profile.headline: Software Engineer II @ Hewlett Packard Enterprise
profile.summary:
Hi, nice to meet you!

I’m a mid-level engineer with 3 years of full-stack development experience. 

My ability to adapt and learn quickly has allowed me to thrive in a fast-paced environment, and enabled me to lead and ship features in a timely manner regardless of existing constraints. I look forward to applying my skillsets to create impactful solutions in my future endeavors.

positions.title: Technical Director
positions.description:
HackDavis is a student-run hackathon at UC Davis with over 600 participants annually, focusing on solving pressing social issues. 

• Developed the HackDavis website in a team of 4 to promote UC Davis' annual hackathon for social good, which attracted 1000+ views
• Built the front-end interface for a custom made team finding tool in a team of 4, which was utilized by 140+ teams and allowed participants to join or create their own team
• Directed a hackathon event with 1000+ participants with a team of 20+ directors  
• Hosted a Python workshop for beginners to introduce fundamental programming concepts through the creation of a text-based adventure game
• Collaborated with the design team to integrate UI/UX components into the front end production code base 

Tech Stack:
Gatsby.js, GraphQL, React.js, Bootstrap, Firebase, CSS, and jQuery

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Nimble Storage dHCI

• Developed the dHCI Sizing Tool which assists users with sizing appropriate dHCI compute nodes by recommending a set of specifications based on their input
• Implemented the user interface in React.js, Typescript, and utilized internal libraries on Grommet and Storybook to ensure UX consistency
• Integrated backend APIs and performed end to end testing using Cypress
• Participated in the Nimble Storage dHCI team standups and sprint meetings and utilized Jira to manage development progress

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Research in browser fingerprinting and computer security under Professor Zubair Shafiq

• Developing machine learning based methods to prevent identity theft by distinguishing between legitimate and malicious intents of fingerprinting 
• Created procedures to identify websites that used bot-detection and developed a program that automatically crawled through 2000+ fingerprinting websites to generate 100+ data points.

Industry collaborators: Mozilla and Apple

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Developed Python scripts utilizing social media location tags, followers, and profiles using Beautiful Soup and Selenium to discover the most viable partnerships, increasing efficiency by 70% 
• Analyzed data on 1,000+ user profiles to generate leads that converted into 50+ potential clients to aid platform development 
• Presented results to key company stakeholders and integrated project into the production codebase
• Coordinated with the marketing team to integrate business insights into the program and tailored features to maximize effectiveness 

Tech stack: Python, Beautiful Soup, and Selenium

projects.title: SilhouScrape
projects.description: SilhouScrape data scrape information about apartments in a designated city, then takes two aspects and creates a scatter plot, each point being a different apartment. Using k-means clustering and silhouette analysis, we clearly identified apartments of more value above its peers.
